News Items 
 
Kildare County Council Publishes 2024 Annual Report 
Kildare County Council has published its Annual Report for 2024, providing an 
overview of the Council’s Programme of Work delivered last year (see pages 9/10). 
 
Register of Electors: New Polling Place 
A new Polling Place is being created in Celbridge Local Electoral Area (LEA), 
following engagement by the County Registrar. St Patrick’s National School in 
Donaghcumper will be added to the LEA as a new polling place (see page 11). 
 
Cities Forum, Krakow  
The Climate Action Office represented Ireland at the Cities Forum in Krakow, Poland, 
held from 17 to 19 June.  This biennial event jointly organised by the European 
Commission (DG REGIO) and the European Urban Initiative (EUI) brought together 
policy makers, urban practitioners, city officials and advocates for sustainable urban 
living (see pages 56/57). 
 
Ireland’s Best Kept Towns Competition 2025  
Naas was successful in the Best Kept Towns Competition achieving the overall title 
of Ireland’s best kept town in the competition. It also won in the best kept large urban 
centre category.  Tribute was paid to the town by Minister Dara Colleary for winning 
both titles (see page 63). 
 
Signing of the Twinning Charter between Rathangan and Freehold, New Jersey 
Members of the Twinning Liaison Committee were delighted to be invited to the 
signing of the Twinning Charter between Rathangan, Co Kildare and Freehold, New 
Jersey.  The event, organised by the Rathangan Freehold Twinning Association, 
took place on Friday 27 June 2025, in Rathangan, Co Kildare (see pages 66/67).

Local Economic and Community Plan (LECP) 
Work continues with the online LECP monitoring tool developed using Microsoft 
Lists. Training is taking place with organisations leading out on actions. A progress 
report will be prepared at the end of 2025 (see page 71). 
 
Transport Operations - Restoration Improvement  
59 road improvement projects covering 50 km of regional and local roads to be 
completed in 2025. Projects are currently at various phases of development 
including design, procurement and construction stages (see page 73). 
 
Into Kildare 
Taste of Kildare was officially launched on 20 June with an event held in the Circle at 
Naas Racecourse, featuring a lunch curated by Lily and Wild. The launch included a 
panel discussion hosted by Santina Kennedy, joined by Aine Mangan and Aisling 
Larkin, who will act as MC for the chef demonstration area across the weekend and 
also deliver her own demo (see page 86). 
 
Erasmus+ Repower Regions  
Kildare County Council, in collaboration with eleven European partners, continues to 
progress the Erasmus+ Repower Regions project, which supports regional 
cooperation and skills development in the heating and cooling sector. Kildare 
recently participated in the international partner meeting held in Riga, Latvia on 26–
27 June, hosted by Riga Technical University (RTU) – a leading institution in 
sustainable innovation in the Baltic region (see page 90).

Recreating History in Athy  
In 2024, artist Anthony Haughey launched Art House Athy – a gallery and workshop 
space on Leinster Street. During his residency, Haughey discovered a powerful 
image by John Minihan, depicting a large gathering in Emily Square in 1987. 
Together, they now invite the people of Athy to help recreate this iconic moment.  On 
Saturday, 19 July at 2:00p.m. (see pages 8/9). 
 
John Devoy Commemoration  
The annual John Devoy commemoration will take place in Naas Library and Cultural 
Centre on 25 September and will include the display of the donated John Devoy 
chair (see page 16). 
 
Budget 2026 
Legislation has passed for a property revaluation for 2026 Local Property Tax (LPT) 
and Revenue will have to be notified of the decision on variation of the Local 
Property Tax (LPT) by 31 August 2025 (see page 22). 
 
The Community Integration Forum 
Meetings are taking place the first Wednesday of each alternative month chaired by 
the Director of Services for Integration with targeted, thematic meetings to address 
specific items on each alternative month. The last CIF meeting took place on the 
Wednesday 04 June 2025 online. The next CIF meeting is scheduled the first 
Wednesday in September 2025(see pages 51/52). 
 
Climate Innovation Fund (CIF) 2025 
The Climate Innovation Fund has been launched with a closing date of 25 July. The 
fund is to provide seed monies to assist with innovation new to Kildare with climate 
action at the core of the proposal (see pages 60/61).

Climate Week:  
The Climate Action Office is preparing to hold Climate Week during the last week of 
October. Given the time of year, they hope to have items that embrace Halloween 
(see pages 61). 
 
Entente Florale 2025 
Judging for Entente Florale took place in Maynooth on Saturday, 12 July.  The day 
was a tremendous success with all the contributors, Tidy Towns, Maynooth 
University and Kildare County Council working together to showcase the town.  
Positive feedback in all categories was received from the judges.  The awards 
ceremony will be in Slovenia in September (see page 63). 
 
Athy Flood Relief Scheme 
There will be a Public Participation Day for the Athy Flood Relief Scheme on 
Thursday 24 July 2025 in Athy library (see pages 64/65). 
 
Play Day 2025 
Play Day will take place on Saturday 06 September from 12.00p.m.-5. 00p.m (see 
page 77). 
 
DeBurghs Woodland Garden 
The gardens have reopened and are now open Thursday to Sunday from 9.00a.m.-
5.00p.m. until the end of October.  No tickets are required this year to access the 
garden (see pages 76/77).

Register of Electors: New Polling 
Place 
 
A new Polling Place is being created in 
Celbridge Local Electoral Area (LEA), 
following engagement by the County 
Registrar. 
  
St Patrick’s National School in 
Donaghcumper will be added to the 
LEA as a new polling place. 
It is proposed to reallocate some 
electors from Scoil na Mainistreach to 
this new polling place. The work of 
identifying relevant electors is ongoing, 
in consultation with the County 
Registrar. 
  
It is intended to implement this for the 
Presidential Election and future 
electoral events. 
It is proposed that the Council, as the 
Registration Authority, will write to 
electors when this change is ready, 
and engage in other advertising, in 
addition to ensuring that polling cards 
advising of the new polling station are 
issued to electors, on the Returning 
Officer’s behalf.

Library and Arts Service 
News and Highlights  
“The library is the temple of 
learning, and learning has 
liberated more people than all the 
wars in history” -  Carl T. Rowan 
 
Library Service Development Plan 
“Building for Tomorrow” – Kildare 2025 
– 2029 was launched on Friday 13 
June at Naas Library and Cultural 
Centre by The Cathaoirleach, 
Councillor Kevin Duffy. This five-year 
plan sets out a transformative agenda 
for Kildare’s libraries, positioning them 
as inclusive, innovative, and 
sustainable community hubs. 
Developed through extensive public 
consultation and guided by national 
strategies such as The Library is the 
Place (2023), the plan reflects the 
evolving needs of Kildare’s growing 
and diverse population. 
 
 
Picnic in the Park   
Betty Maguire from Maynooth 
Community Library held an information 
stand for Kildare Libraries Service at 
Picnic in the Park, Sunday 15 June, at 
the Harbour Field, Maynooth.   
The event was very well attended with 
stands from many different businesses 
and groups. Attendees received 
Kildare Libraries Service keep cups 
and other Kildare Libraries Service 
merchandise. QR codes were on hand 
for people to scan to join the library 
service online.   Betty also 
demonstrated how to download 
the BorrowBox app and how to access 
Library E-Services.   
 
Refugee Week 2025  
To celebrate Refugee Week 2025 and 
its theme of ‘Community as a 
Superpower’, Eamonn from the Library 
Service and the Kildare County 
Council Integration Team presented a 
hands-on workshop where attendees 
could bring their imagination to life. At 
the makerspace in Naas Library and 
Cultural Centre they learned how to 
design their own custom graphic, 
reflecting community, and then printed 
it on a t-shirt or tote bag to take 
home.

As part of Refugee Week, 18 June 
was designated Fáilte Day.  Kildare 
County Council welcomed everyone 
with a video on social media, of council 
staff saying "fáilte" or "welcome" in 
their own languages. The video 
reached a staggering 10,000 views! 
 
Young Reader’s Festival 
Kildare Libraries hosted the annual 
Beyond The Book: Young Readers 
Festival across two weeks in May. 
18 events were held across libraries, 
schools and online over the two 
weeks.  
This year, the programme included 
local debut author Martina Smith as 
well as Alan Nolan, Dave Rudden and 
Maeve Devoy.  
576 children met and engaged with an 
author during our two-week festival in 
their local libraries, classrooms and 
online.  
It is also worth noting that across our 
branches in May, over 705 pre-school 
children attended story time sessions. 
 
Cruinniú na nÓg 
Cruinniú na nÓg, Ireland’s National 
Day of Creativity for children and 
young people, took place on Saturday 
07 June.  Kildare hosted 35 events 
with 1004+ participants across the five 
municipal districts, and activities 
included felt-making, crochet, manga 
drawing, bi-lingual music workshop, 
sensory play sessions, film screening 
and a Teen Slam Poetry recital. 
Maynooth Library partnered with 
Maynooth Castle, Maynooth Scouts, St 
Mary Church of Ireland and St Mary’s 
and Ladychapel Parish to offer a 
Heritage Treasure Hunt around the 
town.   
 
 
Skills for Life 
Naas Library and Cultural Centre 
hosted two well-attended financial 
literacy talks on Bank Fraud and 
Scams and Making a Will for all its 
patrons, and an I.T. and Internet Skills 
course for Naas Men’s Shed. These 
talks and classes were made possible 
by the library service partnering with 
KWETB and Naas Men’s Shed to avail 
of Adult Literacy for Life Funding.

Undercurrents: A Social and 
Ecological Walking Tour of Leixlip  
Kildare Arts Service attended 
Undercurrents: A Social and 
Ecological Walking Tour of Leixlip on 
17 June. This brought Leixlip-born 
artist Ian Nolan and sociologist Dr. 
Eamonn Slater on a journey of 
discovery, unearthing the 
undercurrents of Leixlip’s ongoing 
history and exploring the complex

County Kildare Orchestra  
County Kildare Orchestra performed a 
special concert at the Dreamland 
Ballroom, Athy on 07 June which was 
attended by Kildare Arts Service. This 
concert presented A Galaxy of Sound 
– From Stars to Planets and featured 
music from John William’s Star Wars 
and Holst’s the Planets. County 
Kildare Orchestra is a volunteer 
orchestra based in County Kildare and 
is supported by Kildare County Council 
Arts Service.   
 
Recipient of Short Grass Film 
Commission 2025  
Kildare Arts Service has announced 
Frame It Productions as the recipient 
of the Short Grass Film Commission 
2025. This €14,000 award aims to 
support the production of a short film in 
County Kildare in 2025/2026. Written 
and directed by Margaret Kane-Rowe 
and produced by Frame It Productions, 
‘Holly’ is a short comedy/drama set in 
1985. It follows the story of 12-year-old 
and her relationship with her loving 
father as she finds her way and her 
confidence growing into adolescence. 
‘Holly’ will be filmed on location in 
County Kildare in autumn 2025.
